title: How chemistry broke vitalism
question: How did chemists learn to make life's compounds themselves?
hook: Chemists once believed living things held a secret force, until one 1828 experiment cracked that belief.
idea: Organic compounds can be made from non-living starting materials, which overturned vitalism and opened up the study of carbon's bonding.

beats.prompt: Under vitalism, organic matter needed a vital force. Wöhler started only from inorganic salts, potassium cyanate and ammonium sulfate. What did he get?

choices.label: Nothing, since the vital force was missing
choices.feedback: He made urea from the inorganic salts, with no vital force involved.

choices.label: Only a new inorganic salt
choices.feedback: He produced the organic chemical urea.

beats.explain: Wöhler produced urea from inorganic starting materials, the first time a substance thought to be organic was made without biological starting materials.

items: Chevreul begins studying soaps made from fats (around 1816)
Wöhler produces urea from inorganic salts (1828)
Kekulé and Couper develop chemical structure (1858)
beats.explain: Chevreul came first around 1816, then Wöhler in 1828, Perkin in 1856, and the structure concept in 1858.

beats.prompt: Sort each technique into assessing purity or traditional separation.
beats.explain: Chromatography techniques such as HPLC and gas chromatography assess purity, while distillation, crystallization, and solvent extraction are traditional separation methods.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: Vitalism said organic matter needed a vital force.
Wöhler made urea from inorganic salts, with no biological starting materials.
So a substance thought to be organic was made without life.
Therefore Wöhler himself immediately and confidently declared vitalism disproved.
beats.explain: Wöhler himself was cautious about claiming he had disproved vitalism, though the event is now generally accepted as doing so.
